ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure has three layers of horizontal media, the upper layer labeled n1, the middle layer labeled n2, and the lower layer labeled n3; the two interfaces are parallel to each other, so the normal directions are the same, both vertical directions. The light ray propagates obliquely downward to the right from medium 1 above, and after entering medium 2 it becomes closer to the vertical normal; after entering medium 3 again, the light ray becomes farther away from the vertical normal, propagating almost horizontally to the right. Reasoning: At the first interface, when the light ray enters medium 2 from medium 1, it bends toward the normal, indicating that the refractive index of medium 2 is greater than that of medium 1, that is, n2 > n1, so light is slower in medium 2 than in medium 1, v1 > v2. At the second interface, when the light ray enters medium 3 from medium 2, it bends away from the normal, indicating that the refractive index of medium 3 is less than that of medium 2, that is, n3 < n2, so v3 > v2. It is also necessary to compare medium 1 and medium 3: because the upper and lower interfaces are parallel and the normals are the same, while in the figure the angle between the light ray in medium 3 and the normal is larger than that in medium 1. From Snell's law, it can be known that the refractive index of medium 3 is less than that of medium 1, that is, n3 < n1, therefore v3 > v1. Combining these gives the speeds from fast to slow as v3 > v1 > v2.

raw_record.question_text: A beam of light passes from medium 1 to medium 2 to medium 3 as shown in the diagram. Rank the speed of light in the three media from fastest to slowest.

method.method_draft: First describe the diagram: there are three horizontal layers labeled n1 on top, n2 in the middle, and n3 on the bottom. The light ray travels downward/right from medium 1 into medium 2, then into medium 3. At the first boundary, the ray in medium 2 is closer to the vertical normal than it was in medium 1, so it bent toward the normal; therefore medium 2 has larger refractive index than medium 1 and light is slower in medium 2. At the second boundary, the ray in medium 3 becomes much farther from the vertical normal, nearly horizontal, so it bent away from the normal; therefore medium 3 has smaller refractive index than medium 2 and light is faster in medium 3. Finally compare medium 1 and medium 3 directly: since the interfaces are parallel, they share the same vertical normal, and the ray in medium 3 makes a larger angle with the normal than the ray in medium 1. Thus medium 3 has smaller refractive index than medium 1 and light is faster in medium 3. Conclude v3 > v1 > v2.

Estimate the ray angles with respect to this common normal from the drawing: in medium 2 the ray is closest to the normal, in medium 1 it is at an intermediate angle, and in medium 3 it is farthest from the normal, almost parallel to the boundary.
